reviews.decision_reason: select_demand preserves all supplied corpus rows with demand_score >= 3, carrying record_id, need, demand_score, source_id, and source_weight forward. In this package all 8 input rows meet that threshold, so the function does not introduce an unrelated candidate or drop visible demand evidence at its boundary.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: observed jobs and market-demand support remain visible
generic keyword or unrelated candidates are excluded
missing or contradictory evidence remains visible

reviews.decision_reason: normalize silently truncates the selected demand table to head(len(index_window)) where index_window is [0], reducing 8 retained demand records to only n06-r01. That removes supplied market-demand evidence for n06-r02 through n06-r08 instead of keeping missing or competing evidence visible, and it causes the upstream handoff to contain only one need and one evidence source.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: observed jobs and market-demand support remain visible
claims are supported without hiding missing or contradictory evidence

reviews.decision_reason: assemble_provenance correctly ranks and projects the already-normalized input it receives, but because normalize has already reduced the evidence to one row, this boundary propagates an incomplete provenance handoff. The local transformation is not shown to add unrelated candidates or further discard rows, so the fault is upstream rather than localized here.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: provenance reflects all visible demand support received by the unit
missing or contradictory upstream evidence remains visible in final handoff
generic keyword or unrelated candidates are excluded
